title: Helicity in monoaxial chiral magnets
authors: Victor Laliena, Diego Gironés-Magaña, Javier Campo
abstract: The equilibrium state of a monoaxial chiral magnet surrounded by a non-magnetic medium (such as air or vacuum) is a helical texture characterized by a single, well-defined wave vector. No metastable states have ever been observed in such systems. Recently, however, it was demonstrated that when a chiral magnet is in close contact with two uniaxial ferromagnets, a large number of metastable helical states emerge in addition to the equilibrium state [Phys. Rev. B 109, 214424]. These helical states are distinguished by their wave number (helicity). In the present work, we elucidate the topological origin of the stabilization of these states --a mechanism we term dynamical topological protection-- and investigate their static and dynamic properties. We find that, as a consequence of this dynamical topological protection, the winding number of the helical states remains constant under the application of sufficiently weak magnetic fields and polarized electric currents. Furthermore, when a polarized current is applied to a metastable helical state, a static configuration is reached. This state retains the original winding number, but its winding number density becomes non-homogeneously distributed, concentrating near the interface with one of the ferromagnets. The dynamic response to sufficiently large magnetic fields and currents provides mechanisms to switch between different helical states. Since the magnetic properties depend on helicity, these metastable helical states are highly promising for applications in spintronics and magnonics.
summary: This work investigates metastable helical magnetic states that emerge when a chiral magnet is interfaced with two uniaxial ferromagnets. The authors identify the stabilization mechanism as 'dynamical topological protection' and show that these states can be manipulated by applying electric currents or magnetic fields. This makes the system highly promising for advanced spintronic applications.
main_problem: To elucidate the topological origin of stabilization for metastable helical states in monoaxial chiral magnets when they are placed in contact with two uniaxial ferromagnets.
main_result: The system exhibits metastable helical states stabilized by a mechanism termed dynamical topological protection, allowing switching between these states using magnetic fields and polarized currents.
method: Theoretical analysis involving the derivation of energy functionals and solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation numerically for both static and dynamic configurations.
model_or_system: A composite magnet consisting of a central monoaxial chiral magnet sandwiched between two identical uniaxial ferromagnets. The dynamics are governed by the LLG equation incorporating exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), and anisotropy terms.
key_observables: Helicity (wave number) of helical states, winding number density distribution, and stability spectrum derived from linearized LLG equations.
important_parameters: Chiral magnet parameters ($A_c, D, K_c$) and ferromagnet parameters ($\mu_u, A_u, K_u$); the helicity $p$.
main_assumptions: The system is assumed to have infinite dimensions in $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$; stability analysis relies on linearizing the LLG equation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the composite chiral magnet structure, showing the relative placement of the chiral and ferromagnetic regions along the z-axis.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model (composite magnet), derives the relevant energy functional and dynamics (LLG equation), analyzes the topological origin of metastable states, and investigates their static/dynamic response to external fields and currents.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the study of topologically protected non-equilibrium states and switching mechanisms using current injection shares conceptual links with controlling quantum states in engineered solid-state systems relevant to spintronics.
